title: Flat scalar comparison is the evaluation-normalized resolution roof
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small in the module universe and $\varphi:R\to S$ a morphism of commutative ring sheaves whose ordinary scalar extension $E=S\otimes_R-$ is exact. Use module derived categories, K-flat tensor and normalized derived internal Hom $H_R,H_S$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] [def-coef-ringed-tensor-hom-model] [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Write $Q$ for localization of complexes in $D(R)$ and $U:D(S)\to D(R)$ for termwise restriction of scalars along $\varphi$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Let $P$ be a flat-term K-flat $R$-complex [def-pc-kflat-complex] and $C$ any $R$-complex. In the strict models [def-sfb-internal-hom-strict-models] [def-sfb-internal-hom-strict-roof], put $J=I_R(C)$, $B=\mathcal Hom_R(P,J)$, $F(M)=\mathcal Hom_R(P,I_R(M))$, $a_S:S\otimes_R B\to F(S\otimes_R J)$ and $v_S=F(S\otimes_R\eta_C)$. Then $v_S$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Let $c:E^{\mathbf L}H_R(QP,QC)\to H_S(E^{\mathbf L}QP,E^{\mathbf L}QC)$ be the transpose of scalar-extended evaluation, and let $\Theta$ be the evaluation-normalized scalar-adjunction isomorphism [lem-sfb-dc-hom-scalar-adjunction]. Under the canonical exact-extension representative identifications, $\Theta\,U(c)=[v_S]^{-1}[a_S]$. Equivalently $[v_S]\,\Theta\,U(c)=[a_S]$, with $[\ ]$ denoting localization. This equality is natural in both derived inputs and in compatible maps of coefficient rings; it requires neither finite freeness, filtered continuity nor boundedness.

proof.text: Exactness of $E$ and the natural cohomology comparison give $H^r(Eu)=E(H^r(u))$, so $E$ preserves quasi-isomorphisms. For any complex $M$, choose a flat-term K-flat resolution $T\to M$. The defining K-flat computation of $E^{\mathbf L}QM$ and the quasi-isomorphism $ET\to EM$ identify it canonically with $Q(EM)$. These identifications commute with maps, since both are induced by localization of the same exact functor. Set $e=E\eta_C:EC\to EJ$. It is a quasi-isomorphism. Naturality gives $I_R(e)\eta_{EC}=\eta_{EJ}e$, and both augmentations are quasi-isomorphisms; hence $I_R(e)$ is a quasi-isomorphism between K-injectives. Apply Hom-invariance with first-variable map $1_P$ and second-variable map $I_R(e)$. It gives the required quasi-isomorphism $v_S=\mathcal Hom_R(P,I_R(e))$.

proof.text: Put $A=UEB=S\otimes_R B$, with the actual representative identification understood. Since $J=I_R(C)$, the fixed Hom representative identifies $QB$ with $H_R(QP,QC)$. Apply the K-flat chain-transpose lemma to $1_B:B\to\mathcal Hom_R(P,J)$ and the K-injective target $J$. Thus evaluation into $QC$ is represented by $\operatorname{ev}_J:B\otimes_R P\to J$, $f\otimes p\mapsto f(p)$, followed in the derived category by $[\eta_C]^{-1}$. The order is $B,P$, so no interchange sign occurs. The same lemma applies to the arbitrary complex $A$ and the K-injective target $I_R(EJ)$; $A$ need not be K-flat.

proof.text: Define $h:A\otimes_R P\to UEJ$ by $h((s\otimes f)\otimes p)=s\otimes f(p)$. The scalar chain-identification lemma, with $q=1_{EJ}$, supplies this evaluation map: it is evaluation of $\theta\,U(\sigma_{1_{EJ}})$, hence is a chain map on the actual sheaf tensors and product Hom complexes. The strict normalization of $a_S$ says exactly that its uncurried chain map is $\eta_{EJ}\circ h$: on every slice, degree, Hom-product projection and pure tensor both maps send $(s\otimes f)\otimes p$ to $\eta_{EJ}(s\otimes f(p))$. Such tensors generate the sheafified tensor and the product projections detect equality. The chain-transpose lemma and inverse-augmentation normalization therefore identify the derived transpose of $[a_S]:QA\to H_R(QP,Q(UEJ))$ with $[\eta_{EJ}]^{-1}[\eta_{EJ}h]=[h]$.

proof.text: Here is the tensor representative used when restricting scalar-extended evaluation. Choose a flat-term K-flat resolution $t:T\to B$. On the K-flat pair $T,P$ the normalized scalar tensor comparison is the localization of the actual chain tensor isomorphism. After restriction and insertion of the scalar unit on $P$, its pure-tensor formula is $(s\otimes x)\otimes p\mapsto s\otimes(x\otimes p)$. The chain-transpose lemma makes $t\otimes1_P$ a quasi-isomorphism; exact $E$ preserves this map and $t$. Also $EP$ is K-flat by scalar-extension preservation. Consequently the representative square descends along these quasi-isomorphisms from $T$ to $B$, giving the same displayed formula for $A\otimes_R P$. Composing with $E(\operatorname{ev}_J)$ gives $h$ of step 3. This verifies the representative comparison for the possibly non-K-flat complex $B$; it does not assume that tensoring arbitrary complexes computes a derived tensor.

proof.text: Write $d=\Theta\,U(c)$, with source $QA$ and target $H_R(QP,Q(UEC))$. By the evaluation equation for $\Theta$, its transpose is restricted scalar-extended evaluation after the scalar unit on $P$. Steps 2 and 4 compute it as $[e]^{-1}[h]:Q(A\otimes_R P)\to Q(UEC)$. Postcomposition with $[v_S]$ is the map $H_R(QP,[e])$ under the fixed Hom representatives, because $v_S=F(e)$. Naturality of tensor-Hom transposition in the target makes the transpose of $[v_S]d$ equal to $[e][e]^{-1}[h]=[h]$. This equals the transpose of $[a_S]$ computed in step 3. Injectivity of the closed-adjunction Hom-bijection gives $[v_S]\Theta U(c)=[a_S]$. Since step 1 makes $[v_S]$ invertible, multiplication by its inverse gives $\Theta U(c)=[v_S]^{-1}[a_S]$.

proof.text: For maps $u:P'\to P$ and $w:C\to C'$, the evaluation identities are $\operatorname{ev}_J((f\circ u)\otimes p')=f(u(p'))$ and $I_R(w)(f(p))=(I_R(w)\circ f)(p)$. Naturality of $\eta$ supplies the squares for $e$ and $v_S$; the scalar chain-identification lemma supplies the squares for $h$ under compatible ring maps. Thus the transpose computation commutes with maps of all the complex representatives. It also commutes with inversion of representative quasi-isomorphisms by the chain-transpose lemma and Hom-invariance. Since localization is generated by complex maps and inverses of quasi-isomorphisms, this gives naturality in both derived inputs. The scalar adjunction's coefficient compatibility and the normalized scalar tensor square give the same assertion for compatible coefficient maps (with the flatness assumptions of the statement). Equivalently, the established roof equals the evaluation-defined $d$, whose naturality follows from these squares and injectivity of transposition. No step uses a finite basis, a colimit or a degree bound.
